title: The universal isomorphism locus in the base is open
statement: Let $B,A,C$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $p:A\to B$ and $q:C\to B$ be morphisms, and let $f:A\to C$ satisfy $q\circ f=p$. Assume that $p$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism], locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that $q$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], and a closed map on underlying topological spaces. There is an open subscheme $U\subseteq B$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that, for every scheme $B\prime$ and every morphism $h:B\prime\to B$, the base-changed morphism $f_{B\prime}:A\times_BB\prime\to C\times_BB\prime$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is an isomorphism if and only if $h$ factors through $U\hookrightarrow B$.

source.place: Tag 05XD, spaces-more-morphisms-lemma-where-isomorphism, scheme specialization; all six hypotheses and the universal base-change conclusion.

proof.text: The map $p$ is closed: in the definition of universal closedness [def-weil-proper-morphism], take the identity base change of $B$. Also $p$ is locally of finite type: each local finite presentation in [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] writes its algebra as a quotient of a polynomial algebra on finitely many generators, which is finitely generated as required by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus both properties needed below follow without an extra hypothesis on $p$.

Apply [lem-sfb-universal-surjective-flat-open] to the given $p,q,f$. Its assumptions are precisely the flatness and local finite presentation of $p$, its closedness from Step 1, and the assumed local finite type and closedness of $q$. Obtain an open $U_1\subseteq B$ such that for every $h:T\to B$, $h$ factors through $U_1$ exactly when $f_T$ is surjective and flat.

Apply [lem-sfb-universal-closed-immersion-open] to the same $p,q,f$. Step 1 gives local finite type of $p$; universal closedness of $p$ and separatedness of $q$ are original hypotheses. Obtain an open $U_2\subseteq B$ such that for every $h:T\to B$, $h$ factors through $U_2$ exactly when $f_T$ is a closed immersion.

Let $U$ be the open subscheme corresponding to $U_1\cap U_2$. A morphism $h:T\to B$ factors through an open subscheme $V$ exactly when its underlying image is in $V$: restrict the underlying continuous map and the structure sheaf map to $V$; the resulting morphism is unique since the inclusion identifies its structure sheaf with the restriction [def-weil-open-immersion]. Consequently $h$ factors through $U$ exactly when it factors through both $U_1$ and $U_2$.

Fix an arbitrary scheme $T$ and $h:T\to B$. If $h$ factors through $U$, Steps 2--4 imply that $f_T$ is surjective, flat and a closed immersion. Apply [lem-sfb-surjective-flat-closed-immersion-isomorphism] to $f_T$ to obtain an isomorphism. Conversely, if $f_T$ is an isomorphism, its underlying map is a homeomorphism, hence surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]; its stalk maps are ring isomorphisms, hence flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]; and its structure sheaf map is an isomorphism, hence surjective, so it is a closed immersion onto the whole target [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Steps 2 and 3 then force $h$ to factor through both opens, hence through $U$ by Step 4. This proves the universal equivalence for arbitrary, including nonreduced, $T$ without identifying any fibrewise locus with a universal one.
